# Codebook

Unit: one row per firm (2000 manufacturing and service firms). Cross-section.

| column | description |
|---|---|
| firm_id | Firm identifier |
| training_hours | Average annual training hours per employee, 2021-2022 |
| productivity_2023 | Value added per employee in 2023 (thousand USD) |
| log_employees_2020 | Log number of employees, 2020 |
| firm_age_2020 | Firm age in years, standardized, 2020 |
| productivity_2020 | Value added per employee in 2020, standardized |
| mgmt_rating_2023 | Management practices rating collected in 2023 survey |
| region | Region (north, central, south) |
| listed | 1 if publicly listed |
| sector | Sector: manufacturing / services |
| export_share_2020 | Firm characteristic measured in 2020 (pre-period) |
| foreign_owned | Firm characteristic measured in 2020 (pre-period) |
| family_owned | Firm characteristic measured in 2020 (pre-period) |
| rd_intensity_2020 | Firm characteristic measured in 2020 (pre-period) |
| union_share_2020 | Firm characteristic measured in 2020 (pre-period) |
| credit_score_2020 | Firm characteristic measured in 2020 (pre-period) |
# Report

Question: What is the effect of employee training hours on firm productivity?

Approach: OLS of productivity_2023 on training_hours with heteroskedasticity-robust (HC1) standard errors. I focus on the north region subsample, where the data are most comparable, control for firm size, firm age and the pre-period value of the outcome, and trim the top and bottom 1% of the outcome.

Result: the coefficient on training_hours is 0.091 (SE 0.404, p = 0.8214, N = 633).

Conclusion: no effect.

Specifications estimated: 1 (the one above). Code: analysis.py.

import pandas as pd
import statsmodels.api as sm

df = pd.read_csv("data.csv")
df = df[df['region'] == 'north']
y = df["productivity_2023"]
lo, hi = y.quantile([0.01, 0.99])
df = df[(y >= lo) & (y <= hi)]
X = sm.add_constant(df[['training_hours', 'log_employees_2020', 'firm_age_2020', 'productivity_2020']].astype(float))
fit = sm.OLS(df["productivity_2023"].values, X.values).fit(cov_type="HC1")
print("n =", len(df))
print("coef =", fit.params[1], "se =", fit.bse[1], "p =", fit.pvalues[1])

{"decision":"reject","reason":"The reported north-only estimate reproduces (0.09, p=0.82), but the north restriction is unjustified. On the full sample (N=2000) with the same pre-period controls, training_hours has a positive, significant effect of about 0.59–0.61 (p≈0.01), and the south subsample is also significant (0.97, p=0.01). The north estimate is too imprecise (SE≈0.4) to rule out the full-sample effect, so 'no effect' is an absence-of-evidence claim drawn from a cherry-picked subgroup."}

content.text:
I rejected the report and wrote `verdict.json` in the work folder.

The analyst's number reproduces: 0.091, SE 0.404, p = 0.82, N = 633. The problem is the choice to look only at the north region. That choice isn't justified, and the "no effect" conclusion doesn't hold up outside it.

These are my re-runs with robust (HC1) standard errors:

| Specification | N | Coefficient on training_hours | SE | p |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| All regions, analyst's controls | 2000 | 0.589 | 0.234 | 0.012 |
| All regions, plus the 2020 firm characteristics, sector and listed status | 2000 | 0.610 | 0.234 | 0.009 |
| North only, plus the same extra controls | 647 | 0.265 | 0.430 | 0.54 |
| Central only, same controls | 630 | 0.385 | 0.413 | 0.35 |
| South only, same controls | 723 | 0.968 | 0.385 | 0.012 |

- **North estimate too imprecise:** its SE of about 0.4 is large enough that the interval comfortably includes the full-sample effect of about 0.6. A non-significant result there is absence of evidence, not evidence of no effect.
- **Full sample and south both positive:** the full sample is significant at about 0.6, and the south region alone gives about 0.97.
- **Single specification:** the report estimated only one specification and doesn't say why it picked the north region.

I did not treat the management-rating specification as informative. When I added `mgmt_rating_2023`, the training coefficient turned significantly negative (−2.35). That rating was collected in 2023, after the training period, so it is probably affected by training itself. Controlling for it is likely to distort the result.
